claim.why_it_matters: Indentation is the index's only structure — it is what makes 'FROM phrase 576' a sub-entry of ACCEPT statement rather than a top-level entry, and the only thing distinguishing parentless heads ('ADDRESS OF PROGRAM phrase', 'ADVANCING ON LOCK phrase', 'ALL option', 'Alignment of data') from their children. Flattened to unindented consecutive lines with no trailing double-space or list markers, the block renders as one run-on paragraph: both the parent/child relation and the line structure are lost. This is the first index page; the same flattening runs through the whole index.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, with two corrections to the description. (1) Both quotations are verbatim-accurate. The 300dpi render of PDF page 1234 (printed folio 1204, first index page) shows the right column exactly as quoted: 'ACCEPT statement 292, 480, 512, 576' flush left with 'FROM phrase 576' and 'Screen format 740' indented one level beneath it; 'ACCESS MODE clause 319' flush left with 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 312' indented beneath; 'ALL option' flush left (no page number of its own) with 'FLAG-02 directive 70' indented beneath. I read the printed glyphs directly and the indent step is unambiguous and consistent down the whole column. The markdown side is equally accurate — repr() of specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 66-118 of the page-1234 block shows zero leading whitespace, zero list markers, and zero trailing double-spaces on any of the 112 non-blank lines. (2) The usual refutations do not apply. No text is missing — every entry and every page number is present in correct reading order — so this is not lost content, and it is not a page-break, wrapping, or hyphenation artifact. The reason it survives the 'it is only formatting' objection is decisive and internal to the document: THE TRANSCRIPTION ITSELF ENCODES THIS EXACT INDENTATION ELSEWHERE. Page 1237 renders the identical PDF construct as '    CLASS clause [382](#page-382)' under the parentless head 'BOOLEAN phrase'. Sweeping the whole index (pages 1234-1259), 10 pages (1237-1239, 1243, 1247-1248, 1253, 1255-1256, 1259) carry 26-53  -indented lines each, while 16 pages including 1234 carry zero. So the flush-left rendering on page 1234 is not a document-wide convention or a Markdown limitation — it is an inconsistency against the transcription's own established mechanism, and on this page the hierarchy information is genuinely absent from the file rather than merely re-encoded. The meaning change is concrete: 'FLAG-02 directive 70' reads as a top-level index entry rather than as the ALL-option sub-entry it is, and 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 312' reads as a locator for FILE-CONTROL itself rather than for the ACCESS MODE clause as it appears in that paragraph. Mitigating context, not a refutation: the index is non-normative back matter, so no COBOL semantics or conformance judgement can be corrupted by this — the practical cost is degraded navigation, which is why 'structural' is the right severity but the priority is low.
verdict.corrected_description: Kind is mislabeled: nothing is misplaced, duplicated, or missing. Every index entry and page number on page 1234 is present in correct source order. The actual defect is DROPPED SUB-ENTRY INDENTATION — the transcription omits the '    ' prefix that marks an index sub-entry, so children collapse to the same level as their parents and parentless heads ('ADDRESS OF PROGRAM phrase', 'ADVANCING ON LOCK phrase', 'ALL option', 'Alignment of data') become indistinguishable from their children. Two statements in the claim's rationale need correcting. First, 'the same flattening runs through the whole index' is false: the index spans pages 1234-1259, and 10 of those 26 pages (1237-1239, 1243, 1247-1248, 1253, 1255-1256, 1259) DO correctly encode the indent as four   entities. The defect affects 16 pages (1234-1236, 1240-1242, 1244-1246, 1249-1252, 1254, 1257-1258). That inconsistency is the strongest evidence the flush-left form is a defect rather than a deliberate convention, and it supplies the exact repair format. Second, the 'renders as one run-on paragraph / line structure is lost' rationale is real but is NOT the page-1234 discrepancy: no index page uses hard line breaks (page 1237 and page 1234 both have 0 lines ending in two or more spaces), so every index page collapses into a single rendered paragraph, including the correctly indented ones. Line-break loss is a separate, index-wide issue to file once; the page-1234 finding is solely the missing indent prefix. Severity 'structural' is apt for the hierarchy loss, but note the index is non-normative back matter — no normative text, syntax diagram, or general rule is affected, so this is a low-priority navigational defect.
